title: Embeddings and Vector Stores
description: Understand how text becomes vectors, how similarity search works, and which stores fit .NET backends.

blocks.text: An embedding is a list of floating-point numbers that captures the meaning of a piece of text. Two texts with similar meanings produce vectors that are close together in vector space. This property makes it possible to search for ideas instead of exact keywords.

You send text to an embedding model, and the model returns a fixed-size vector. The length depends on the model; for example, many models return vectors of length 1536 or 3072. Longer vectors can carry finer nuance but use more storage and compute.

blocks.title: Conceptual embedding call in C#
blocks.content: You do not need exact code yet; this shows the shape of the operation.

blocks.title: Common distance and similarity metrics
items: **Cosine similarity** — measures the angle between vectors; widely used and scale-invariant.
**Euclidean distance** — measures straight-line distance; useful when magnitude matters.
**Dot product** — fast and common in optimized stores; related to cosine when vectors are normalized.

blocks.title: Start simple
blocks.text: For learning, pgvector in a local PostgreSQL instance is often enough. For production, consider managed vector search with strong filtering and security controls.

items.question: Do I need to understand the math behind embeddings?
items.answer: Not deeply. Know that similar meaning maps to nearby vectors, and that your choice of model and store affects retrieval quality.

items.question: Can I use multiple embedding models?
items.answer: Yes, but keep query-time and index-time models consistent within one searchable collection.

items.question: Are embeddings enough for semantic search?
items.answer: Often combined with keyword filters or hybrid search for best precision and recall.

blocks.title: Compare Two Embeddings
blocks.description: Use any provider to embed two sentences with similar meaning and inspect their cosine similarity.
steps: Choose a local or cloud embedding model.
Embed the sentence: The server returned a 500 error.
Embed a semantically close sentence and a semantically distant sentence.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should see higher similarity for sentences with similar meaning, confirming the core idea behind vector search.
